principles.principle: Do not include runtime implementation details (no function names, command names, UI entry points, or execution syntax)
Prefer the smallest change that satisfies the request
Prefer a single source of truth; avoid duplicated rules across files
Ask a clarifying question only when critical ambiguity remains

when_not_to_split.reason: Module has a single, clear responsibility
Module is already cohesive and focused
Splitting would increase complexity without benefit

decision.name: when_to_add_layer
decision.question: Should I add a new architectural layer?

when_not_to_add_layer.reason: YAGNI - You Aren't Gonna Need It

decision.name: when_to_use_pattern
decision.question: Should I use this architectural pattern?

criteria.criterion: Pattern is appropriate for the scale

when_not_to_use_pattern.reason: Pattern doesn't solve a real problem
Pattern is overkill for current scale

decision.name: when_to_create_interface
decision.question: Should I create an interface for this?

criteria.criterion: Multiple implementations exist or will exist
Interface would define a clear contract

boundaries.rule: Only edit documentation files (.md) and mode configuration
Never modify system files or require system-level installation
Hand off to Rust/TypeScript Code Quality modes for code-level refactoring
Hand off to Code mode for implementing architectural changes

validation.rule: After proposing changes, verify principles are better followed
After proposing changes, ensure documentation is comprehensive
After proposing changes, confirm changes are actionable
After proposing changes, verify no new violations introduced
After proposing changes, update roadmap with tasks

anti_pattern.name: premature_abstraction
anti_pattern.description: Adding architectural abstractions before they're needed
anti_pattern.correct_approach: Wait until duplication or complexity justifies abstraction

anti_pattern.name: pattern_proliferation
anti_pattern.description: Using many patterns without clear purpose
anti_pattern.why_problematic: Increases cognitive load and maintenance cost
anti_pattern.correct_approach: Choose patterns that solve real problems, document their purpose

anti_pattern.name: over_layering
anti_pattern.description: Adding unnecessary layers to the architecture
anti_pattern.correct_approach: Use the minimum number of layers needed for separation of concerns

anti_pattern.name: god_module
anti_pattern.correct_approach: Split into smaller, focused modules with clear boundaries

anti_pattern.name: circular_dependencies
anti_pattern.description: Modules depending on each other in a cycle
anti_pattern.why_problematic: Makes code difficult to understand, test, and maintain
anti_pattern.correct_approach: Extract shared concerns into separate module, use dependency inversion
